tb21_profile.skill: Cross-compile a real multi-file C codebase for a foreign ISA: obtain/select a MIPS toolchain, repair the Makefile and the target's libc/ABI assumptions, and link an ELF that a third-party emulator will load and run with working stdout and file I/O
tb21_profile.domain: GCC/musl cross toolchains, GNU Make, MIPS ELF and ABI, doomgeneric's platform shim, a JS MIPS emulator (vm.js)
tb21_profile.task_form: build/packaging under cross-compilation, verified end to end by running the artifact under the emulator

verifier_notes: No grade I disagreed with. Two notes for the merge: CalibForge's cross-compilation slate is unusually well pinned for a build task (software-engineering_20260604_002443_013 has 9/9 substantive assertions, 20260604_003814_013 has 10/11), which for this genre means the tests run the cross-built artifact rather than just checking it exists. On the other side, TerminalWorld's tw_105217 (a compiled-and-packaged Maven build, a plausible-looking match) is FREE and is excluded. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is entirely absent-graded as expected, but it is the corpus with the most on-topic content after CalibForge, so its lack of verification actually costs something here -- I kept rts_task_24702e8563eef351a1c3cedd in the final ten because no graded task in the pool combines build, file-says-it-is-the-right-machine, and run-under-emulator as directly.

Cross-compile a vendored source tarball for aarch64 and make it usable under QEMU user-mode emulation; configure-plus-cross-build.

notes: CalibForge is far and away the best corpus for this task: it has a dedicated cross-compilation family (RISC-V64 and arm-linux-gnueabihf builds run under QEMU, bare-metal RISC-V with no libc, a glibc-free custom-stdlib build, a node-hosted foreign-ISA interpreter) that the v1 pool has almost nothing comparable to, and it is strongly verified. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is the surprise second place -- despite being the boilerplate-heavy corpus, it contains a real cluster of aarch64 cross-toolchain, qemu-user, Makefile-and-verify and Emscripten tasks; it is all absent-graded, so treat its entries as unverified. Terminal-Lego contributes one strong win (task_00421, installing a cross-compiler toolchain) plus solid ELF/static-linking/build-system background. TMax is decent but only generically: hundreds of fix-the-broken-Makefile tasks, none cross-architecture. TerminalWorld's ranks 8-10 are quota filler scored 1 -- it has three or four usable build tasks and no more. SWE-Smith is genuinely useful here for an unexpected reason: the whole conan family is cross-compilation toolchain logic (GNU triplets, AutotoolsToolchain flags, per-arch environments), so judge it on skill/domain and accept the task_form penalty; I put its best entry in the final ten. No task in the entire 76k pool targets MIPS specifically -- every cross-compilation match is RISC-V, ARM64 or WebAssembly.
